vo: Making ads is half the job. Running them is the other half, and that's a different skill.
Create one more channel called Management, and add your studio Bot to it.
Then create a second Bot, Ads Manager. Its title: launches and watches our ad campaigns.
Now one room has two teammates: one that makes the ads, and one that runs them.
In the Management channel, write one message: launch my three new cold brew ads on Meta.
The studio Bot hands over the files. The Ads Manager picks them up and asks one question back.
Put all three in one ad set, same budget, so they compete fairly? Yes.
If something is missing, like a Facebook page that isn't connected yet, it tells you instead of guessing.
Then it fills in the campaign: platform Meta, objective sales, a test budget of twenty-five dollars a day.
It still waits for your OK before anything goes live. You stay the one who spends the money.
Set a hard limit in the request too: never spend more than twenty-five dollars a day without asking me. Bots follow written boundaries.
After launch, the two Bots keep talking: which ad is winning, which hook to try next.
The three numbers to watch: how many people stop scrolling, how many click, and what each sale costs you.
Give the Ads Manager a simple rule: after three days, pause the weakest ad and move its budget to the best one.
Then turn it into a routine. Every morning at nine, the Ads Manager posts a short report, and the Studio Bot makes two new versions of the winner.
That's the loop: make, test, keep the winner, make more like it. The Bots run it; you read one message a day.
Now, the mistake I promised. It's letting the AI say things your product can't back up.
In the US, the FTC banned fake reviews and testimonials, and it named AI-generated ones on purpose.
And Meta reviews every ad against its advertising standards. Break them often enough and your ad account gets restricted.
So three rules: no made-up results, no fake 'I've used this for years' stories, and label AI content where the platform asks.
Write the lines as a scene, not a testimony. 'Here's my morning with it' is honest. 'It cured my tiredness' is not.
That's the full factory: find a winner, break it down, recreate it, make three, and launch with a second Bot.
Start small. One Bot, one reference ad, one product photo. You can have your first ad before lunch.
